text: Once the staggered private sale discounts of up to fifty percent are counted as a cost of capital, the cost structure of an ICO is arguably significantly higher than that of an IPO, notwithstanding the ICO's lower legal and offering expenses.
citation: Kaal, Digital Asset Market Evolution (2020). SSRN: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=3606663
abstract: Considering these steep discounts to incentivize earliest possible investments, the cost structure of ICOs is arguably significantly higher than the cost structure of an IPO.

additionalProperty.name: scope_conditions
value: ICOs conducted in 2017 and 2018 with staggered discount structures
comparison against average IPO underwriting fees of four to seven percent
